limited_overlap.description: applicants with prior_earnings between 44,820 and 719,670: 83% of the 2401 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.

applicants with months_unemployed equal to 0: 55% of the 1337 training applicants there have an enrolment propensity outside the overlap bounds, so the effect for them rests on the outcome model rather than on comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants.
applicants whose follow-up earnings are not recorded: their effect is identified only if non-response is unrelated to earnings given the adjustment set and enrolment (1971 training applicants).

warnings: Enrolled and non-enrolled applicants differ in pre-enrolment columns: mean prior earnings 18,110 against 37,158; the estimates adjust for the columns listed under roles.
experience is an exact linear combination of the other pre-enrolment columns; it is not put in the adjustment set, and its information is carried by the columns it is built from.
Candidates ['months_unemployed'] passed the joint-test rule, but the R-learner smooth on them does not beat a constant effect by more than one SE (gain 74,022, SE 76,368); none is claimed.

No covariate passed the claim rule (joint p below 0.05 in the primary fit, at the median of four nuisance fits, with one sign). Candidates by median joint p: months_unemployed p=0.0295 (-1026, -862, -1374, -1341 dollars per SD); parttime p=0.0562 (-2238, -1331, -2061, -1752 dollars per SD); smsa p=0.341 (+1232, +1282, +743, +708 dollars per SD); education p=0.412 (-103, -338, -504, -579 dollars per SD). The joint p-value of each covariate moved across fold splits (the single-split fit gave p near 0.004 for age and 0.03 for prior earnings), so no covariate is claimed as an effect modifier.
18.7% of training rows have a cross-fitted propensity outside the overlap bounds; the all-rows ATE depends on the outcome model in those rows, and the overlap-bounded estimate is 3,922 dollars.
Instrument check (distance_km, responders only): complier effect 1,986 dollars with 90% interval [-7,688, 11,660], against the ATE 4,451. The complier effect and the ATE are different quantities.
Certificate and hours worked are measured during or after the program and are mediators; they are not adjusted for, so the estimates are total effects that include the paths through them.

Test applicants differ from training applicants in means: prior_earnings 31,224.8 (train) against 25,877.1 (test); months_unemployed 2.7 (train) against 3.1 (test). Per-applicant effects for test applicants outside the training range are extrapolated.

Test applicants outside the propensity overlap bounds: 6.9%. 157 of the 800 applicants at the top of the cate order are among them; their effects come from the outcome model, not from comparable enrolled and non-enrolled applicants. Restricting the top group to the overlap region gives 800 applicants with mean cate 4,767 dollars.
Test applicants outside the training range of an effect-model term: 1.3%.

No covariate passed the modifier rule, so no effect modifier is claimed. The per-applicant effects and the ranking come from a model on the lead covariates ['months_unemployed', 'parttime', 'smsa'], whose evidence is weak; the ranking carries less information than the interval widths suggest.
